parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The module has one file, session.repository.ts, and it passes the rule. It covers a single concern: the Mongoose-backed implementation of the SessionRepository port, in the class SessionDocumentRepository. Every method that turns stored records into domain objects, or domain objects into stored records, goes through SessionMapper.toDomain or SessionMapper.toPersistence. No method returns raw Mongoose documents. All data access goes through the injected Model<SessionSchemaClass>.

There is one minor overlap inside the file. The list of protected fields (id, createdAt, updatedAt, deletedAt) is spelled out twice: as delete statements in update() and as an Omit<> type in updateByHash(). These are local and serve different purposes (removing fields at runtime vs. a compile-time type limit). It is not a real business rule copied into a second place. Also, updateByHash writes only payload.hash and ignores any other fields in the payload. That is a possible correctness problem, not a cohesion or boundary problem. Neither issue makes the file fail the rubric.
